text.title: Cohort Implementation Worked Example
text.summary: One complete cohort config for a BigQuery warehouse: login as the retention event at offsets 1 / 7 / 14 / 30 / 60 / 90, an incremental model keyed on cohort_week / day_offset / user_id with a 90-day lookback, the two dbt tests, a chart spec with the May 4 cutoff and null immature cells, and five computed cells including one that is not yet mature, with a note on each non-obvious value; then the config as it is usually written and what the validator prints.

section.title: Scenario
section.p: A B2B SaaS keeps `stg_users` and `stg_events` in BigQuery with identity resolved in staging. Growth wants a weekly retention curve per signup-week cohort read at 1, 7, 14, 30, 60 and 90 days, with "login" as the retention event. Data is pulled on 2026-05-04.

example.title: cohort_retention_weekly on BigQuery
example.code: { "settings": {"warehouse_engine": "bigquery", "retention_event": "login", "day_offsets": [1, 7, 14, 30, 60, 90], "week_start": "monday", "timezone": "UTC"}, "sources": {"users_table": "stg_users", "events_table": "stg_events", "user_id_column": "user_id", "identity_resolved_upstream": true, "signup_ts_column": "signup_ts_utc", "event_ts_column": "event_ts_utc"}, "model": { "name": "cohort_retention_weekly", "materialized": "incremental", "unique_key": ["cohort_week", "day_offset", "user_id"], "partition_by": "cohort_week", "lookback_days": 90, "cohort_week_expr": "CAST(DATE_TRUNC(DATE(signup_ts_utc), WEEK(MONDAY)) AS DATE)", "join_condition": "event_ts_utc >= signup_ts_utc", "denominator_source": "users_table", "retention_event_declared_in": ["sql", "schema_yml", "settings"] }, "tests": {"not_null": ["cohort_week", "day_offset", "user_id"], "accepted_values": {"column": "day_offset", "values": [1, 7, 14, 30, 60, 90]}}, "chart": {"data_cutoff": "2026-05-04", "x": "cohort_week", "series": "day_offset", "metric": "retained_users / cohort_users", "immature_value": null, "render_immature_as": "blank"}, "cells": [ {"cohort_week": "2026-01-05", "day_offset": 90, "cohort_users": 1502, "retained_users": 240, "retention": 0.16}, {"cohort_week": "2026-03-30", "day_offset": 1, "cohort_users": 1810, "retained_users": 1050, "retention": 0.58}, {"cohort_week": "2026-03-30", "day_offset": 7, "cohort_users": 1810, "retained_users": 706, "retention": 0.39}, {"cohort_week": "2026-03-30", "day_offset": 14, "cohort_users": 1810, "retained_users": 543, "retention": 0.3}, {"cohort_week": "2026-03-30", "day_offset": 30, "cohort_users": 1810, "retained_users": null, "retention": null} ] }
example.note: `cohort_week_expr` is BigQuery's `DATE_TRUNC(..., WEEK(MONDAY))` over `signup_ts_utc`, because BigQuery's default week starts on Sunday and a local-time column would move Sunday-night signups between cohorts (r-cohort-key-signup-week-monday-utc). The join is on `user_id` with identity resolved in staging, so a user who signs up on mobile and logs in on desktop is one retained user (r-stable-user-id-not-anonymous). "login" appears in the SQL filter, in the schema.yml description and in `settings.retention_event`, which is what `retention_event_declared_in` records (r-retention-event-defined-once, r-settings-declare-engine-event-offsets). `tests.accepted_values.values` is the same list as `settings.day_offsets`, so an offset that exists only in a dashboard fails the build (r-fixed-day-offsets-enforced-by-test). The join condition excludes imported events dated before signup (r-only-events-after-signup-count). `lookback_days` is 90, the largest offset, so the incremental run still sees a January cohort's day-90 logins (r-incremental-key-partition-and-lookback). Every cell divides by the cohort's 1,810 or 1,502 signups from the users table; day-1 retention is 0.58, not 1.0 (r-denominator-is-full-cohort). The March 30 cohort's day-30 cell is null: its last signup day, April 5, plus 30 days is May 5, after the May 4 cutoff, while the January 5 cohort's day-90 cell (April 11) is mature (r-incomplete-cells-null-not-zero).

example.title: the same model as usually written
example.note: What the validator prints: `user_id_column` is `distinct_id` with identity unresolved (r-stable-user-id-not-anonymous); `signup_ts_column` does not end in `_utc` and `cohort_week_expr` names no Monday week start (r-cohort-key-signup-week-monday-utc); `denominator_source` is `model_rows` (r-denominator-is-full-cohort); `retention_event_declared_in` lacks schema_yml and settings (r-retention-event-defined-once); `not_null` lacks `user_id` (r-incremental-key-partition-and-lookback); `chart.immature_value` is 0 and `render_immature_as` is zero (r-incomplete-cells-null-not-zero). Once those are fixed the cross-field checks add: `lookback_days` 30 is below the largest offset 90, so day-60 and day-90 events for older cohorts never land (lookback-shorter-than-max-offset); `accepted_values.values` [1, 7, 30] differs from `settings.day_offsets` (r-fixed-day-offsets-enforced-by-test); the day-1 cell has 1,050 cohort users and 1,050 retained, a 100 percent retention that only a row-count denominator produces (row-count-denominator); the day-30 cell for the March 30 cohort is not mature on May 4 and carries 0 instead of null (immature-cells-as-zero); and the third cell has `cohort_week` on a Wednesday with `day_offset` 3, which is in neither the Monday grid nor the offset set (r-only-events-after-signup-count). What the reviewer sees: a chart whose newest cohorts plunge to zero every week and whose day-1 line sits at 100 percent.
